job.title: SDE2 - Full Stack
job.description:
About the role

We're hiring two backend-heavy full-stack engineers (SDE 2 or SDE 3) for the Cowork team at Sarvam. Cowork is the agentic side of Indus: users hand it real work, and an agent plans, uses tools and connectors, works in a cloud sandbox, and hands back files, docs and artifacts across web, Android, iOS, macOS and Windows.

The role is full stack, but the centre of gravity is the backend: the BFF that every client talks to, and increasingly the agent harness behind it. You'll ship features end to end, from the API and data model through to the client screens on mobile, desktop and web.

What you'll work on

Most of your time goes into the BFF and the services around it; the rest into client work and the harness, depending on what the roadmap needs that quarter.

 - BFF (Chat Service): design and own the APIs that web, mobile and desktop share: sessions, conversations, streaming turns, artifacts, connectors, custom and managed agents. Data modelling, migrations, auth and RBAC, pagination and search.

 - Real-time streaming: stream LLM output, tool calls and agent events from the harness to clients over an event bus, and keep it correct under reconnects, retries and partial failures.

 - Agent harness and platform: contribute to Panja, our agent harness: tool and MCP integrations, sandboxed execution, file and artifact flows, latency and token-cost work.

 - Clients: build features end to end on our Kotlin/Compose Multiplatform apps (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows) and the Next.js web app, so a feature you design in the backend reaches users on every surface.

 - Production ownership: observability, on-call, RCAs, and making the system faster and cheaper with numbers to back it.


Tech stack

Python and PostgreSQL are the core; you don't need every item below on day one.

 - Backend: Python, SQLAlchemy + Alembic, PostgreSQL, OpenAPI

 - Supporting services: Go

 - Mobile and desktop: Kotlin Multiplatform + Compose Multiplatform (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows)

 - Web: Next.js, React, TypeScript


What we're looking for

A strong backend engineer who has also shipped real frontend work and is happy to keep doing both.

 - 3+ years (SDE 2) or 5+ years (SDE 3) building and running production backend services.

 - Deep in at least one backend language; Python preferred, Go, Kotlin/JVM or TypeScript/Node also welcome.

 - Solid API and data-model design: REST/streaming APIs, PostgreSQL schema design, migrations, indexing, transactions.

 - Distributed-systems fundamentals: async processing, queues or event streams, idempotency, retries, failure handling.

 - Production experience on Kubernetes or a similar platform, with observability you actually used to debug an incident.

 - Has shipped user-facing features on at least one client platform: Android, iOS, desktop or web (React/Next.js). Kotlin/Compose experience is a plus, not a gate.

 - Willing to pick up the side of the stack they know less, and to learn agent and LLM systems on the job.

 - Clear written communication: design docs, PR descriptions, RCAs.

Nice to have

 - Built on LLM APIs: tool calling, streaming, prompt caching, evals, or an agent loop of your own.

 - MCP servers or clients, OAuth connector integrations, or sandboxed code execution.

 - Kotlin Multiplatform / Compose Multiplatform, or native Android/iOS.

 - Real-time systems: WebSockets/SSE, NATS, Kafka, or Temporal-style durable workflows.

 - Go services, or performance and cost work with measurable before/after numbers.

 - Open-source work or public writing we can read.

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

What's more, Cloudflare operates within 50 milliseconds of 95% of the Internet-connected population globally (for context, the blink of an eye is 300-400 milliseconds!). We are passionate about making the Internet more secure, reliable, and faster for everyone.

Cloudflare’s Engineering teams build and run the software that handles the massive amount of traffic that flows through our network. We also have teams that build the UI and control plane for our software, using modern patterns and libraries in a microservices-based architecture. Technologies include: Typescript/Javascript, Go, Rust, C/C++ and Python.

The ideal intern is passionate about making the Internet a better place. You will work alongside experienced engineers. You will push code this internship that touches hundreds of millions of web surfers. We like to get things done, so we are looking for interns who are curious, proactive, and able to complete projects. This is a great opportunity for engineers who want to learn to develop at Internet scale.

You can check out our internship blogs to learn more about our program and hear directly from our past interns.

• Work cross-functionally with various teams.

• Work closely with a mentor to guide you through the internship and help with career goals.

• Build your network across the company through our various in and out of office socials, networking programs, Employee Resource Group (ERG) programs, and Activity Groups.

• Present your project to the entire company at the end of the internship.

• Connect and learn from our executives and leadership team including our co-founders.

• Learn and develop skills through our professional development workshops.

• Write for our Cloudflare blog and be featured on Cloudflare.tv sessions.

Desirable Skills, Knowledge and Experience

• Currently pursuing a degree or program in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics or relevant field to the role.

• Demonstrated critical thinking skills and drive to learn and adapt new technologies.

• Curiosity, empathy and ability to get things done.

• Ability to commit to a full-time (40 hours/week Monday - Friday) for a minimum 12 week internship.

• In office 3-5 days a week in Lisbon, PT.

Bonus Points

Demonstrated passion for software development, such as personal projects, open-source contributions, or experience with our developer platform using Cloudflare for Students.

job.title: Senior Software Engineer - Data Infrastructure
job.description:
THE ROLE

Sarvam's products produce events, model traces, evals and billing data, and need to read that data back. The Data Platform team builds and runs the central data infrastructure every product uses: ingestion, streaming, the analytical warehouse, transformations, access control and audit.

We are hiring a Software Engineer / Senior Software Engineer (2–5 years of experience) to own this platform end to end. You will design, build and run systems that other teams depend on in production, and make real decisions on database internals, streaming and platform design. Stack: Go/Python, ClickHouse Cloud, Kafka, Avro, Airflow, dbt, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN & DO

 - Build and run the ingestion path: the service every product sends events to, Kafka behind it, and the pipes that land data in ClickHouse within seconds. Own schema validation, rate limits, dead-letter handling and the client SDKs.

 - Own the warehouse: ClickHouse Cloud. Design tables for the read path (sorting keys, partitions, materialized views, TTL), separate compute per workload, set per-user limits and per-tenant isolation, and attribute cost to the team that spent it.

 - Build reliable data pipelines and solve data problems: dbt models and Airflow DAGs with the BI engineers, CDC from product databases, sync and backfill jobs that are safe to re-run, and the data problems product teams bring you, such as a late source, a number that doesn't match or a query that has slowed down.

 - Make the platform self-serve: a registry of every dataset with its owner, schema, freshness and access; provisioning and permissions as code.

 - Run it in production: everything as Terraform and Helm with metrics, traces and alerts; be on call; handle incidents end to end, write the RCA and fix the root cause.

 - Grow the platform: new products keep arriving. You will help decide what the platform should do next and build it, whether that is a new source or sink, or a new way for teams to use the data.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 2–5 years of experience building, shipping and running large-scale, data-intensive systems in production, ideally at a startup where you owned things and were on call for them.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of: an OLAP database (ClickHouse preferred; Druid, BigQuery or Redshift also fine) or Kafka / event streaming. You understand how a columnar store writes, merges and scans data, or how a partitioned log gives ordering and delivery guarantees.

 - Experience with large-scale messaging systems like Kafka or RabbitMQ: partitions, consumer groups, delivery guarantees, backpressure.

 - Good at Go, or good at Python.

 - You know the usual data-system problems: schema evolution, idempotency, backpressure, partitioning, retention and TTL, CDC.

 - You have built or run at least one of: an event pipeline, a transformation layer (dbt, Spark or SQL on Airflow), a provisioning or control-plane service, or a multi-tenant data service with access control.

 - Comfortable with AWS, Kubernetes and Terraform in production.

 - You test before shipping, debug with metrics and traces, write RCAs, and document what you build.

 - Passion for data infrastructure and for enabling others by making their data easier to access.


NICE TO HAVE

 - ClickHouse in production: MergeTree, materialized views, projections, quotas, settings profiles, row policies, ClickHouse Cloud.

 - Kafka in depth: MSK, Kafka Connect, schema registry (Glue or Confluent), Avro.

 - dbt and Airflow at scale.

 - Audit or security data systems: append-only logs, integrity checks, tenant isolation.

 - OpenTelemetry, LLM observability (Langfuse or similar), eval pipelines.

 - Built an internal platform that other teams adopted.
